name: 85 mm f/1.4 (patent example, Sigma large-aperture medium-telephoto)
representativeSource: camera-wiki.org "Lens patents" table (row: JP2011170128, FF SLR, "Sigma DG 85 mm f/1.4 EX HSM", filed 2010.02.19, published 2011.09.01, SIGMA CORP, inventor Yamamoto Yukihiro), https://camera-wiki.org/wiki/Lens_patents, accessed 9/28/2026; matched by photonstophotos.net Optical Bench Hub row "JP2011-170128 Example05P Sigma 85mm F1.4 EX DG HSM". Corroborated structurally: our transcription of Numerical Example 5 has 11 elements in 8 groups, matching Sigma's published "11 Elements in 8 Groups" spec.

source.location: [Lens specification] / [レンズ諸元] table under Numerical Example 5

asph.convention: patent prints kappa (K) directly with K=0 meaning no added conic term, same convention as k here

surfaces.label: L11 rear; t = BF at infinity, DERIVED (patent prints 'B.F.' symbolically with no numeric value; see notes)

gaps.note: patent's close-focus condition: 'shooting distance 0.85 m'; index 5 = patent surface 6, the sole variable gap (single moving front sub-group between the two negative-preceded positive triplets).

focus.minFocusSource: Sigma 85mm F1.4 EX DG HSM spec page, https://www.sigma-global.com/en/lenses/85_14/, accessed 9/28/2026 ("Minimum Focusing Distance: 85cm / 33.5in.")

iris.source: Sigma 85mm F1.4 EX DG HSM spec page, https://www.sigma-global.com/en/lenses/85_14/, accessed 9/28/2026 ("Number of Diaphragm Blades: 9 Blades (Rounded Diaphragm)")

notes: This patent's tables never print a numeric back focal distance: every example's last surface row prints the literal text 'B.F.' (or 'BF') instead of a number, in both the Japanese original and the English machine translation. No other table in the document (no separate 'total length' or 'various data' section) supplies it either.

Because of that gap, the last surface's t (39.87 mm) is DERIVED here by our own paraxial y-nu trace through the other 19 surfaces (see .local/lens-normal/selfcheck.py), not copied from patent text. `stated.bf` is left unset because the patent does not state it; the self-check for this lens therefore checks EFL against the patent's f=83.58 only, not BF against a patent figure.
Patent gives no effective-diameter column; all `sd` values are our own paraxial-trace estimates.
Single aspheric surface (patent 10, the front face of L6); K, A4, A6, A8, A10, A12 all printed, A12=0.
